scenario: The skill delegates lifecycle enforcement to the shared controller.
failureMode: The skill reinvents transitions or evidence handling.

scenario: The skill starts from persisted state before editing.
failureMode: The assistant starts a new loop and loses required work.

scenario: The skill forbids score-driven matrix changes.
failureMode: The assistant weakens an evaluator to make a candidate pass.

scenario: The skill guards durable Markdown before rewriting it.
failureMode: A durable loaded skill document is edited without the required protected-token backup and validation transaction.

scenario: The skill keeps command grammar and routing governance in one Usage contract.
failureMode: A skill creates an ambiguous, detached, or duplicate command router.

scenario: A skill documents delegated command or information routes outside Usage without creating a second invocation catalog.
failureMode: Skill Manager either rejects a necessary owner-specific options table or permits a duplicate invocation router.

scenario: The skill owns linked prose, correct local links, and ignore-aware review scope.

assertions.expected: ## Review scope, prose, and link integrity

failureMode: A review stops at SKILL.md, follows broken or wrong-owner guidance, or includes ignored runtime state.

scenario: The skill review includes project and coding-assistant AGENTS policies as additional static consumers and verifies their inheritance.
failureMode: A global skill change leaves project or coding-assistant policy stale or treats it as a second parent policy.

scenario: The skill does not restore provider-driven training.
failureMode: The skill silently depends on an unavailable provider workflow.

scenario: Project and coding-assistant policy boundaries remain explicit.
failureMode: A local policy becomes a second global policy or silently replaces its parent.

scenario: A skill maintenance run must keep one reviewed matrix unchanged across baseline, candidate, and challenge.
failureMode: A candidate silently changes its evaluation matrix or reuses stale evidence while appearing green.

scenario: A discipline-enforcing skill must be tested against observed failures before and after repair.
failureMode: The maintainer writes plausible guidance without proving that it changes the failure behavior.

scenario: A skill test must resist rationalization and distinguish wording evidence from deployment closure.
failureMode: A single green receipt or score is mistaken for robust behavioral evidence and closure.

scenario: Skill Manager owns and documents the shared seven-part skill contract for every package.
failureMode: The owner skill omits usage, lifecycle inputs, ordering, proof, or evaluation boundaries from the shared contract.

scenario: An existing skill is rewritten as one seven-section document instead of receiving a detached template wrapper.

assertions.expected: rewrite the entire source in place

failureMode: The maintainer satisfies the heading count by adding a fluffy seven-section preamble while leaving the old skill body detached.

scenario: Skill Manager rejects a universal exact-output persona when a skill requires judgment, research, interaction, or delegation.
failureMode: The reusable contract suppresses legitimate uncertainty or delegated ownership in favor of a brittle persona.

scenario: A heading-count pass is not enough when old instructions remain as a detached second half.
failureMode: The review declares success from seven headings while duplicated legacy prose or filler remains outside the real contract.

scenario: The skill applies the Agent Skills package, progressive disclosure, and description constraints.
failureMode: A skill package violates the upstream format or uses a vague, over-broad trigger description.

scenario: Description optimization generalizes beyond the prompts used to tune it.
failureMode: The maintainer tunes a description to one-shot prompts or exact failed-query keywords and mistakes that for reliable triggering.

scenario: Output evaluation compares clean configurations and combines assertions, deterministic checks, human review, and cost data.
failureMode: The maintainer reports a green score without proving skill value, reviewing outputs, or accounting for cost and flakiness.

scenario: Bundled scripts are usable by non-interactive agents and composable in the workflow.

assertions.expected: what the agent should try next

failureMode: A script hangs, hides its interface, emits unparseable output, or gives an agent no recovery path.

scenario: The package keeps description as the only activation owner and documents the optional caller hint boundary.
failureMode: Description activation is missing or a second trigger field is allowed to compete with it.

scenario: Description activation is evaluated with balanced realistic positive and negative queries from a maintained set.
failureMode: The maintainer relies on keyword inspection or a few obvious prompts instead of observing real skill invocation across balanced cases.

scenario: Every skill exposes a clear usage contract and explains its ordered route with a plain-text diagram before prose.
failureMode: The skill hides invocation syntax or forces the reader to reconstruct the normal route from disconnected prose.
